mainTopic: How מעשר בהמה can be separated without exact counting, and the search for the source of רבא's rule that the tenth animal becomes holy on its own
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a proof supporting רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds that an animal separated as מעשר בהמה without proper counting is still valid. The chain runs like this. תרומה can be separated by estimate and by thought. The Torah calls מעשר 'תרומה', so the same is true of מעשר. A היקש then carries the rule over to מעשר בהמה. Next, רבא rules that the tenth animal becomes holy by itself (עשירי מאליו הוא קדוש), even if it is never named or taken out of the pen. The גמרא searches for רבא's source and tries four ברייתות. The first three are rejected, because in each case something else could explain the ruling: the animal was called 'holy', it left the pen or was pointed at, or the flock was exempted by מנין הראוי. The fourth ברייתא says outright that a tenth left in the pen is מעשר. But it clashes with another ברייתא that calls the mistakenly named ninth animal חולין. A תנא before רב ששת resolves the clash by assigning one ברייתא to רבי שמעון בן יהודה, and his words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: מעשר is called תרומה, so it can also be separated by estimate and thought
steps.stepSummary: The rule that תרומה can be separated by estimate and by thought also applies to תרומת מעשר and to מעשר, because the Torah calls מעשר 'תרומה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, תרומת מעשר may be taken by estimate and by thought. And the Torah calls מעשר 'תרומה', as it is written: 'For the tithe of the children of Israel, which they set apart as תרומה to ה׳, I have given to the Levites as an inheritance.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of a proof. It shows that the easy way of separating תרומה (by estimate, or just by thinking) also works for מעשר, because a פסוק calls מעשר 'תרומה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא אלעזר בן גומל taught that תרומה does not need exact measuring. It can be set aside by estimate (אומד) or even by thought alone (מחשבה). Because the פסוק uses the word 'תרומה' for מעשר, the same easy method carries over to מעשר. This is the first link in a chain that will end with מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion the לוי gives to the כהן from his tithe
Estimate; separating without exact measuring
Thought; separating just by deciding in one's mind
The Torah (literally, the Merciful One) called it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the derivation from the previous daf supporting רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר may be separated by estimate and by thought, just like תרומה

steps.title: Animal tithe is linked to grain tithe, so it too can be separated without counting
steps.stepSummary: A היקש links מעשר בהמה to מעשר דגן. So just as grain tithe can be separated by estimate and thought, animal tithe can be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And animal tithe is compared to grain tithe. Just as grain tithe is separated by estimate and by thought, so too animal tithe is separated by estimate and by thought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the chain. It uses a Torah comparison (היקש) to bring the easy separation rule from grain tithe over to animal tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed the rule applies to מעשר דגן. Now the היקש between מעשר בהמה and מעשר דגן (learned earlier from 'עשר תעשר') moves the rule to animals. So an animal set aside as מעשר without a proper count can still be valid, which supports רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Was compared (by היקש); two topics are linked in the Torah, so they share rules
Animal tithe; every tenth animal is holy
Grain tithe

steps.whatToRemember: The chain is: תרומה, then מעשר (called תרומה), then מעשר בהמה (through the היקש). All of them can be separated by estimate and thought, without exact counting.

phrases.english: And animal tithe is juxtaposed to grain tithe.

steps.title: רבא rules that the tenth animal is holy by itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא states that the tenth animal becomes holy on its own, even if it was never counted out loud or taken from the pen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The tenth animal is holy by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבא says that once nine animals were counted, the tenth becomes holy automatically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the owner counts each animal as it leaves the pen and calls the tenth 'עשירי'. רבא holds that even if the tenth stays in the pen and is never named, it is still holy as מעשר. Holiness comes from the counting process itself, not from naming the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: The tenth animal
By itself; automatically
Holy; has the status of a sacrifice

phrases.english: Rava says:
The tenth is sacred of its own accord.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: עֲשִׂירִי מֵאֵלָיו הוּא קָדוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic about how מעשר בהמה becomes holy
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After nine animals are counted, the tenth becomes holy as מעשר even without being named or leaving the pen.

steps.title: Where does רבא learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source רבא is relying on.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does רבא know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבא's source. This is a setup line: next, the גמרא will try out possible sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real request for a source, not an attack on רבא. The following steps propose four ברייתות, one after another, and test whether each one really proves his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know?

phrases.english: From where does Rava derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the statement in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבא's rule that the tenth is holy by itself

steps.title: First suggestion: a ברייתא that the tenth is holy even if not called עשירי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבא learns his rule from a ברייתא: the tenth is holy even if the owner did not call it 'עשירי', because the פסוק says 'the tenth shall be holy' in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he learns it from what was taught: 'I only know the case where he called it "tenth". If he did not call it "tenth", from where do we know? The verse says "the tenth shall be holy", meaning in any case.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a first source for רבא. A ברייתא says the tenth is holy even without being called 'tenth', so perhaps naming is never needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אילימא' ('if you say') signals a suggestion that will likely be rejected. The proposed logic: if the tenth is holy even when not named 'tenth', then naming does not matter, and the tenth is holy even if it stays in the pen.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a suggestion that will likely be rejected
That was taught in a ברייתא
The verse teaches
In any case

phrases.english: If we say from that which is taught:
I have only where he called its name 'tenth'.
If he did not call its name 'tenth', from where do we know?
The verse states: 'The tenth shall be holy',
in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא teaches that the tenth is holy even if not called 'tenth', so perhaps naming is never needed

steps.title: Rejection: maybe he called it 'holy' instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion. Maybe the ברייתא means he did not say 'tenth' but did say 'holy', so some speech still took place.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is 'tenth' that he did not call it, but he did call it 'holy'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the first source. The ברייתא may only mean that the specific word 'tenth' was not needed, not that no words at all were needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case the owner says nothing about the tenth animal. In the ברייתא, the owner may still have called it 'holy'. So the ברייתא cannot prove that a silent, unnamed animal in the pen is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps; introduces a rejection
Holy; here, a word the owner may have said

phrases.english: But perhaps it is 'tenth' that he did not call it,
but he did call it 'holy'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed source in step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the first ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may involve calling the animal 'holy', which is a form of designation that is missing in רבא's case

steps.title: Second suggestion: the ninth was mistakenly called tenth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different source. If someone called the ninth animal 'tenth' and then the real tenth came out while he stayed silent, the real tenth is still מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from what was taught: If he called the ninth 'tenth', and the tenth came out and he did not speak, the ninth is eaten once it has a blemish, and the tenth is מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second source for רבא. Here the real tenth became holy even though the owner said nothing about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ninth animal, wrongly called 'tenth', gets partial holiness. It is eaten only after it develops a מום. The real tenth became מעשר with no words spoken, which looks like רבא's rule that the tenth is holy by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new attempt
The ninth animal
Eaten once it has a blemish
And he did not speak

phrases.english: Rather, from that which is taught:
If he called the ninth 'tenth',
and the tenth came out and he did not speak,
the ninth is eaten with its blemish,
and the tenth is tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first source was rejected, offers a second source
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that the tenth is holy even without speech
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about calling the ninth animal 'tenth'

steps.title: Rejection: there the tenth came out or was pointed at
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second source. In that case the tenth actually left the pen and was singled out, or the owner pointed at it, which is not true in רבא's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is different there, because the tenth was singled out for him. Or alternatively, because he pointed at it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof as well. In the ברייתא something marked the tenth animal: it came out of the pen, or the owner pointed at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's case is a tenth animal that stays in the pen with nothing marking it. In the ברייתא the tenth was identified, either by leaving the pen or by being pointed at. So the ברייתא does not prove that a completely unmarked tenth is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
Was singled out or clearly identified
Alternatively
He pointed at it

steps.whatToRemember: The first two suggested sources for רבא fail. In each one, the tenth animal was marked in some way: it was called 'holy', it came out of the pen, or the owner pointed at it. רבא's case has no such marking at all. The search continues in steps 9 and 11.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there,
since the tenth was clearly identified for him,
or alternatively, because he pointed at it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאִיבָּרַר לֵיהּ עֲשִׂירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed source in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the second ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the ברייתא the tenth was identified by leaving the pen or by being pointed at, unlike a tenth that stays in the pen

steps.title: A third attempt: the tenth animal died in the pen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a new source. If the ninth was called 'tenth' and the real tenth died in the pen, all the animals are exempt. Maybe this is because the tenth became holy by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from this ברייתא: Someone called the ninth animal 'tenth,' and then the real tenth died in the pen. The ninth may be eaten only after it gets a blemish, and all the other animals are exempt. Why are they all exempt? Isn't it because the tenth became holy by itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The first two sources were rejected, so the גמרא brings a third ברייתא to support רבא. In this case the real tenth animal died while still inside the pen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tenth never left the pen and was never named, yet the ברייתא says the rest of the flock is exempt from מעשר. The גמרא suggests the only explanation is that the tenth became holy all by itself while in the pen. That would be exactly רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The pen where the animals are kept and counted out one at a time
Eaten only once it gets a blemish. This is the rule for a holy animal that cannot be offered.
Exempt from the obligation to tithe
Became holy

phrases.english: Rather, from that which was taught in a baraita:
He called the ninth animal "tenth,"
phrases.notes: He made a mistake while counting.

phrases.english: and the tenth animal died in the pen
the ninth may be eaten only once it gets a blemish,
phrases.notes: Calling it 'tenth' by mistake gave it some holiness.

phrases.english: and all the others are exempt.
What is the reason all are exempt?
Is it not because the tenth became holy on its own?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 rejected the second source, this offers a third one.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that the tenth animal becomes holy on its own, even inside the pen and without being named
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which the tenth died in the pen and the whole flock is still exempt

steps.title: The exemption may come from a fit count
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The animals may be exempt simply because they were counted in a count that could have reached ten, as רבא himself teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they are exempt because they were counted in a fit count. After all, רבא said: a fit count exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 9. It offers another reason why the animals are exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא has a separate rule called מנין הראוי. Once animals are counted in a group that was able to reach ten, they are exempt, even if the tenth is later lost. So the exemption does not show that the tenth became holy in the pen.

keyTerms.meaning: A fit count: a counting that was able to reach ten
Exempts
But perhaps. This opens a rejection.

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different rule of רבא from the one being searched for. One rule says counting exempts the animals. The other says the tenth becomes holy by itself. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: But perhaps they were exempted through a fit count,
for didn't Rava say:
A fit count exempts!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא where the tenth died in the pen
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The exemption can be explained by מנין הראוי. It does not require the tenth to have become holy.

steps.title: A fourth attempt: the tenth stayed in the pen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא. When the ninth was called 'tenth' and the real tenth stayed in the pen, the tenth is still מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from this ברייתא: Someone called the ninth 'tenth,' and the real tenth remained in the pen. The ninth may be eaten only after it gets a blemish, and the tenth is מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings yet another ברייתא to support רבא. This time the tenth animal simply stayed inside the pen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ברייתא says outright that the tenth is מעשר, even though it never left the pen and was not named. That matches רבא's rule directly. The point is not just an exemption, so מנין הראוי cannot explain it away.

keyTerms.meaning: Remained behind
The tithe animal, holy as מעשר בהמה

phrases.english: Rather, from that which was taught in a baraita:
He called the ninth "tenth,"
and the tenth remained in the pen
the ninth may be eaten only once it gets a blemish,
and the tenth is the tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10 rejected the third source, this offers a fourth one.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that the tenth becomes holy on its own inside the pen
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the tenth, which remained in the pen, is מעשר

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the ninth is not holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction. Another ברייתא says the mistakenly named ninth is ordinary and not holy at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא that the ninth is חולין, ordinary and not holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from step 11 by quoting a different ברייתא that rules the opposite about the ninth animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11's ברייתא says the ninth has holiness and can be eaten only with a blemish. This other ברייתא says the ninth is חולין. The two sources disagree, so the גמרא must explain who holds what.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught? This introduces a contradicting ברייתא.
Ordinary, not holy

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: the ninth is non-sacred!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 11 that the ninth is eaten only with a blemish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different ברייתא says the ninth is חולין, which contradicts step 11.

steps.title: A תנא identifies the author as רבי שמעון בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A תנא in front of רב ששת explains that one of the ברייתות follows רבי שמעון בן יהודה. He then begins quoting that ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught in front of רב ששת: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון בן יהודה, as it was taught: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון:
steps.whatsHappening: The contradiction is answered by saying the ברייתות follow different תנאים. This line sets up the next move: the actual words of רבי שמעון בן יהודה continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of forcing both ברייתות to agree, the answer assigns one of them to a specific author with his own opinion about a mistakenly named animal. Once we see that רבי שמעון בן יהודה holds a different view, the two sources no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter of ברייתות taught. These were scholars who memorized and recited the ברייתות.
Whose opinion is this?

In the name of
